subject: Transportation Systems
title: What Counts as High-Speed
description: A micro-lesson that makes What Counts as High-Speed usable.

hook.text: Not every fast train is high-speed rail. There's an official threshold, and it surprises most people.

buildup.text: The International Union of Railways defines high-speed as 155 mph on upgraded lines or 190 mph on new ones.

discovery.text: At those speeds, trains compete with short-haul flights when you factor in airport time.

twist.text: Most 'high-speed' services in the US, like Amtrak's Acela, rarely hit true high-speed thresholds.

climax.text: Only about a dozen countries operate trains above 190 mph in regular passenger service.

punchline.text: High-speed rail has a speed limit—just a very high one.

quiz.question: What speed qualifies as high-speed rail on new dedicated lines?
